subject: Epoch zipper apportionment discrepancy — usage ledger delta
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@ledgerops.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Unexpected apportionment delta in Nov epoch zipper run

Hi Ben,

We noticed a ~9% delta between the usage reported on the dashboard and the CSV ledger exported for our November epoch 'zipper' run. The dashboard shows 1,232,410 token-units for the window, but the export total in column 'apportioned_units' sums to 1,124,780. That gap aligns with a small subset of tenant IDs that were re-apportioned during the nightly zipper job — see attached sample (epoch-zipper-usage-sample.csv) and the screenshot (billing-window-delta.png).

Can you confirm whether those re-apportionments should be billable under our postpay plan? Historically, we only billed final apportioned totals, but the dashboard earlier in the day was reflecting pre-zipper counts and that's what appears on the invoice. Our November invoice is currently on hold with our accounting team until we reconcile.

Thanks — Lena
Billing Ops | LedgerOps Inc.
---
attachments: epoch-zipper-usage-sample.csv (csv, 28 KB), billing-window-delta.png (png, 112 KB)

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@ledgerops.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T10:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected apportionment delta in Nov epoch zipper run

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear examples and the attachments.

Short answer: it depends on timing and the billing ledger used to generate the invoice. Our pipeline runs three steps: (1) streaming meter capture (near-real-time), (2) nightly zipper/apportion job that consolidates across tenants and prefixes, and (3) invoice generation which is supposed to read the final apportioned ledger snapshot.

I pulled the invoice generation logs for 2026-11-01 and I see that the job picked snapshot v20261101-02:12 (pre-zipper) due to a transient retry ordering issue with the snapshot writer. That would explain why your invoice reflects the pre-zipper counts.

I'm looping in Kimberley (CC) from our billing team to validate whether we should re-run invoicing or issue a credit. Quick clarifying question for your team: did LedgerOps run any downstream re-partitions or tenant merges during 2026-11-01 that would cause the nightly zipper to materially change totals? If so, include the merge IDs.

I'll follow up within the hour with recommended next steps.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@ledgerops.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T10:27:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected apportionment delta in Nov epoch zipper run

Thanks Ben — no tenant merges from our side during that midnight window; only a few routing-tag updates for a staging namespace (TAG-88). The sample rows I attached show tenant_id and request_id for the affected lines. We have the internal changelog if you need it.

If re-invoicing is necessary we can approve a one-off reissue on our end provided the net effect is a credit (we were billed more than final apportioned).

— Lena

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@ledgerops.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T11:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected apportionment delta in Nov epoch zipper run

Kimberly / Marissa — quick context: LedgerOps' November invoice appears to have been generated against a pre-zipper snapshot (v20261101-02:12) instead of the final apportioned snapshot (v20261101-03:20). Resulting overcharge ~9% on token units. Lena confirmed there were no tenant merges on their side.

Proposal options:
- Option A: Issue a retrospective credit equal to the delta and keep current invoice (fast).
- Option B: Void and reissue the invoice using the correct zipper snapshot (more thorough; will reflow accounting and could impact any automated payment runs LedgerOps has).

If we do Option A, we need Marissa to confirm the GL account for the credit and whether it should be applied to next invoice or refunded. If Option B, we need to ensure downstream accounting systems at LedgerOps will accept a reissued invoice (Lena indicated they can approve a reissue if it's a credit).

Marissa — can you advise preferred path and GL?

— Ben

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@ledgerops.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T15:04:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected apportionment delta in Nov epoch zipper run

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the billing job traces and confirmed: invoice LO-8721 used snapshot v20261101-02:12. The final zipper snapshot v20261101-03:20 shows the apportioned total of 1,124,780 token-units as Lena reported.

Given LedgerOps' note that a reissue is acceptable if we net a credit, I recommend Option B (void & reissue) because it keeps the audit trail clean and matches our invoicing policy of billing final apportioned snapshots. Steps we will take:
1) Void invoice LO-8721 in our billing system (creates reversal entry).
2) Generate corrected invoice LO-8721-R1 referencing snapshot v20261101-03:20.
3) Apply any automated refund only if LedgerOps requests a cash refund; otherwise we will post credit to account and have it applied to next cycle.

Lena — please confirm whether LedgerOps prefers a cash refund or account credit. Also confirm whether your AR team needs any specific note on the reissued invoice (e.g., "Corrected for snapshot mismatch; previous invoice voided").

Kimberly — I flagged GL code 4302 (Billing adjustments) for the adjustment; please escalate if you want a different code.

Once Lena confirms, we'll start the reissue and notify collections to pause any automated payment attempts for LO-8721 until the reissue is complete.

Best — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
---
